about: Written by hand from CLAUDE.md and the crates' own docs. generate.py checks that every workspace package has an entry, with a layer that exists and a kind it knows, and that no entry names a package that is gone. layers: the rows of the map, top to bottom: where in the system a crate sits. Each crate: its layer; its kind, what sort of crate it is, checked by kinds.py; its concern in plain words; and what it must not do. A crate's must_not is given only where CLAUDE.md states one.

layers.title: Programs
layers.about: What runs: the kkt command, and the dev-only programs that assemble the same crates another way.

layers.title: Assembly
layers.about: Putting the server together from its parts.

layers.title: Surfaces
layers.about: What callers reach over HTTP: the MCP endpoints, their text, and the web page.

layers.title: Access
layers.about: Who is let in at all, who a caller is once in, and which host names the server answers to.

layers.title: Core
layers.about: Every decision and change, and the notices they send.

layers.title: Data
layers.about: The store and the database under it.

layers.title: Operations
layers.about: Settings, setup, services, Docker, Tailscale, client configs, diagnostics, backups and lane files: running kkt on a machine.

layers.title: Clients
layers.about: kkt as a client of a server: the shared MCP client and `kkt watch`.

layers.title: Foundations
layers.about: Time, randomness, names, the stop signal, limits, provenance and logs: what everything else is built on.

layers.title: Dev-only
layers.about: Never in a release: test scratch folders.

kashkeshet.title: kkt (package kashkeshet)
kashkeshet.concern: The `kkt` command and everything it does on a machine: its subcommands and the files and environment they read, the settings and config file, the setup record, key files, how a client reaches the server, and one module per command that takes plain inputs.
kashkeshet.must_not: Hold a clap type outside `cli.rs`, or let a command take one.

kkt-keymode.concern: A second program that assembles key mode again from the shared crates with none of the `kkt` program's code, to show the crates are a core and `kkt` one product on it. The HTTP-only end-to-end tests run against it in CI. Dev-only, never released.
kkt-keymode.must_not: Be released, or share code with the `kkt` program.

kkt-fake-product.concern: The shared crates assembled as a product other than kkt would assemble them, with two swarms and a fake `Identify` mapping made-up bearers to (swarm, role). Its tests check that nothing of one swarm reaches the other. Dev-only, never released.

kkt-web-preview.concern: The web page over simulated data, for working on the page: kkt-web's page over kkt-api-sim's simulated application and stand-in gate, with the real clock, randomness and stop signals, served alone through kkt-server and kkt-server-listen. Its flags and their checks (`SettingError`). Dev-only, never released.

kkt-operate.concern: The operator's commands and this machine's setup record and key selection; effects and lazy serving facts are supplied through OperateParts.
kkt-operate.must_not: Choose native implementations, depend on an effect or another assembly, or parse command-line flags.

kkt-server.concern: Assembling the server around the program's `Arc<dyn AdminApi>` in `Parts`: `/mcp`, `/mcp-admin` and the web page; its `ServerSettings` returns an opaque `CheckedSettings` snapshot for `Parts::new` and composes owner checks and run-record lines with the program's plain values, with `SettingError`; the public adapter from admission and identity to the web gate; the page's sessions; the web page alone over its API and gate (`page`).
kkt-server.must_not: Make decisions: it only wires parts together. It does not choose who a caller is; the program passes `Identify` and the admission modes in.

kkt-server-listen.concern: Binding the server's assembled App to its socket and serving it.
kkt-server-listen.must_not: Decide how the server is assembled.

kkt-mcp.concern: The agent and admin MCP tools, what the two share, their HTTP transport, and what agents are told about each tool.
kkt-mcp.must_not: Touch the database except through the rules, hold tool text in Rust, or decide who a caller is except through `Identify`.

kkt-web.concern: The human's pages, over the operator's operations (kkt-api-operator's `OperatorApi`) in each viewer's swarm, rendering the kkt-api crates' records. Its own contract is only `Gate`, which says who is viewing each request (a swarm and an operator) and whom a key signs in; every change is a checked form post. It keeps the limits only the page applies (`PageLimits`). It keeps its own sessions: their IDs, hashing, expiry, sign-out and form tokens; its own settings, defaults, bounds (`Problem`, `Settings::problems`) and run-record lines (`Settings::record_lines`).
kkt-web.must_not: Depend on the rules, the store, admission or identity: kkt-server adapts them to its gate.

kkt-identity.concern: Who a caller is, as a contract: `Identify` turns an admitted caller's `Principal` into the swarm it acts in and its actor, or a refusal. The one place that decides who someone is and what they may do. A stand-in, `testing::FixedIdentify`, is behind `testing`.
kkt-identity.must_not: Touch HTTP: each surface reads the principal off its own requests.

kkt-identity-keymode.concern: Key mode's identity: `KeyMode`, which implements kkt-identity's `Identify` directly. It decides who a caller is from the key that let it in and the avatar's token, in the one swarm a key-mode server has.

kkt-admission.concern: Whether an HTTP caller is let in at all, and as which `Principal`: no key, which of the server's keys, or (for another program's `Identify` to judge) any bearer token, and for the web page whether sign-in is needed and whom a key admits. Also the checks on the server's keys, and where the access key file goes by default, in the config folder it is given. The admin name file's binding to its key and the advice about it.
kkt-admission.must_not: Know about agent tokens or channel access.

kkt-admission-os.concern: Server key-file texts, private key writes, admin-name text writes and staged-key moves.
kkt-admission-os.must_not: Choose admission rules, select a randomness provider, or word each program's key refusals.

kkt-hosts.concern: Which host names the server answers to.

kkt-api-agent.concern: What any registered agent may do: Api and its areas (Agents, Channels, Messages, Memory, Lanes), with the Limits they enforce; and the records every level shares: the agents, channels, messages, memory and lanes the operations take and give back, the queries they take, who acts, and the errors they return.

kkt-api-operator.concern: What the human who runs the server may do, by area (Views, Changes, Lanes, Server), with the records only they use, the notices the operator hears as things happen (Notice and Notices, from Views::subscribe), and OperatorApi, every operation the operator may use in one swarm. It depends on kkt-api-agent for the shared records.

kkt-api-admin.concern: What /mcp-admin's administrator does: the admin reads across every channel of a swarm (Admin), creating a swarm (Swarms), AdminChannel, and AdminApi, every operation /mcp-admin uses in one swarm.

kkt-rules.concern: Every permission decision and every change, for agents and the operator, each in one swarm; and starting them for a server run (`start`), which records the run first.
kkt-rules.must_not: Reach the database except through its storage module's `Reader` and `Writer`, or format output.

kkt-mcp-formatter.concern: The MCP tools' results turned into text or JSON, within the response size cap: `Formatter`, `Format`, its `Settings` and `MIN_RESPONSE_BYTES`; its own settings, defaults, bounds (`Problem`, `Settings::problems`) and run-record lines (`Settings::record_lines`).
kkt-mcp-formatter.must_not: Decide permissions or read the database.

kkt-events.concern: Notices of new messages, agents, channels and members, and of hidden agents and channels: one bus for the server, each notice heard only in its swarm, with a buffer per swarm kept only while it has a subscriber.
kkt-events.must_not: Let a tokio type out of the crate.

kkt-db.concern: The database contract, for any database: values, tables, keys and constraints; a narrow language of questions and changes (not SQL); transactions; what a search asks for and finds; migrations as additions; the traits a backend implements.
kkt-db.must_not: Know a product's tables, name a database, or use a database library, except in its testing stand-in (FastPlace, on SQLite in memory).

kkt-db-sqlite.concern: kkt-db over SQLite, the only crate that knows SQLite: it opens a SQLite database, in a file or in memory, as a kkt-db `Backend`, running its work on tokio's blocking pool, adopts a database from before kkt-db as the caller's `Legacy` describes, and copies a database for backups.
kkt-db-sqlite.must_not: Know a product's tables, or let a rusqlite type out of the crate.

kkt-config-file.concern: The config file's format: parsing its TOML into `Config`, what the file says in its own terms, and adding an allowed host to its text, with its own error; where the config file is (`config_dir`, `config_file`), under a supplied config-home folder.
kkt-config-file.must_not: Read or write files, or know the settings' checks beyond each value's kind.

kkt-config-file-os.concern: The config file's bytes, and the instructions file's: reading and writing them whole, as plain functions the program calls.

kkt-setup.concern: `kkt setup`: what this machine is set up as, the setup record, and what follows from it: whether `kkt serve` may run here, which server this machine's clients use, and what status, upgrade, lanes, backup, key files and `kkt doctor` do; where kkt's data goes (`data_dir`, `default_db`), from kkt-machine's `Env` and `Platform`.
kkt-setup.must_not: Read files or run anything directly: the program adapts native providers and carries out what is decided here.

kkt-setup-os.concern: Setup's record and unfinished note, data folder, program paths and PATH checks on this machine.
kkt-setup-os.must_not: Decide what setup does or where its files belong.

kkt-service.concern: Running kkt as a service under launchd or systemd, choosing its manager from the supplied optional home and config-home paths (`Manager::for_this_os`), and the plan of what the service runs, from the settings it needs, which the program gives and checks.
kkt-service.must_not: Touch the machine except through its `System` contract.

kkt-container.concern: Running kkt in Docker: its Compose files, its folder, and the commands that set it up, start, back up, upgrade and stop it.
kkt-container.must_not: Decide what a person wants, remember what was set up, or touch the machine except through `Host`.

kkt-container-os.concern: The machine's Docker commands, files and terminal: plain OsHost methods, adapted by the program.

kkt-remote-access.concern: Sharing a service-mode server over the machine's existing Tailscale login.
kkt-remote-access.must_not: Change the Tailscale login, DNS preferences, kkt's config or its service.

kkt-remote-access-os.concern: The machine's tailscale command: plain OsHost methods, adapted by the program.
kkt-remote-access-os.must_not: Decide how the server is shared.

kkt-client-config.concern: MCP client configs and their file formats, so `kkt connect` can add kkt to a client.

kkt-client-config-os.concern: The machine's client-config files and claude command: plain OsHost methods, adapted by the program.

kkt-diagnostics.concern: `kkt doctor`'s checks and their plan, and setup's wait for a new server.
kkt-diagnostics.must_not: Change anything, or touch the machine except through `Prober`.

kkt-diagnostics-os.concern: The machine's key files and diagnostic HTTP probe, returning its own records.
kkt-diagnostics-os.must_not: Let reqwest types out of the crate.

kkt-backup.concern: Backup folders: their names, contents, file modes, and pruning; its own settings, defaults, bounds (`Problem`, `Settings::problems`) and run-record lines (`Settings::record_lines`).
kkt-backup.must_not: Read the clock or copy the database itself: the caller passes both.

kkt-backup-os.concern: Writing immutable backup layouts and removing old folders selected by the backup logic.
kkt-backup-os.must_not: Choose backup names, contents, modes or retention.

kkt-lane-files.concern: Lanes as files: the `<lane>.md` format, reading and writing a folder of them, and the folder's git commit.
kkt-lane-files.must_not: Touch the machine except through `Disk` and `git::Git`.

kkt-agent-client.concern: The shared MCP client, agent credential and watch-state files, plain Http requests for test callers, and reaching the server as an agent or admin.
kkt-agent-client.must_not: Choose the credential-file rule or warning output; implement kkt-watch's contract: the program adapts its records and failures.

kkt-watch.concern: `kkt watch`: waiting for an agent's new messages (or every channel's, as admin) and the line printed for each. The server, clock, saved place and output are injected.
kkt-watch.must_not: Reach the server, the time, its place or its output except through what is injected.

kkt-search.concern: Search as text: the words of a text (FTS5 `unicode61`'s rule, with its word table), a search's terms, whether a text matches them, and an excerpt around the matches, drawn with the marks and window it is given. Pure text: it knows no database.

kkt-hash.concern: Hashing: `sha256`, the SHA-256 digest of some bytes. The one crate that uses sha2; its users call it.

kkt-clock.concern: Time: the Clock contract, Time and Span values, time formatting and FixedClock behind testing. The real clock is in kkt-clock-system.
kkt-clock.must_not: Let a chrono type into its public surface.

kkt-names.concern: Avatars' handles, channel IDs, the name packs, and the operator and admin names with their rules. It draws randomness through kkt-entropy's `Entropy`, with its own character sets.

kkt-entropy.concern: The randomness contract `Entropy`, with `random_chars` as a provided method that takes the alphabet to draw from, and its test doubles behind `testing`.

kkt-entropy-os.concern: Randomness from the operating system: `OsEntropy`, which implements kkt-entropy's `Entropy` directly, a shared contract.

kkt-machine.concern: Facts about the machine: `Env` (the home folder, the folders the environment names, and the base of per-user config they give) and `Platform`, and `Machine`, which gives them, with a stand-in behind `testing`. The crates that place files on the machine take these facts; none reads them.
kkt-machine.must_not: Read the environment, or hold any of kkt's paths.

kkt-machine-os.concern: The machine's facts as this process sees them: `OsMachine` reads the environment and the platform, and implements kkt-machine's `Machine`. The program wires it in.

kkt-shutdown.concern: The stop signal (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM) and the `Shutdown` that ends the server.
kkt-shutdown.must_not: Let a tokio-util type out of the crate.

kkt-log.concern: Structured log events: their level, target, message and named values.
kkt-log.must_not: Know a logging library or perform I/O.

kkt-terminal-os.concern: The terminal's input, output and terminal detection, the closed-output-pipe default, and the browser login link.
kkt-terminal-os.must_not: Decide setup answers or depend on setup/container logic.

kkt-logs.concern: Log levels, policy checks, rollover and age-pruning rules, as pure plans.

kkt-logs-os.concern: Writing log files, starting the tracing subscriber, and TracingLog over the shared log contract.
kkt-logs-os.must_not: Choose rollover or pruning rules; read a real clock itself.

kkt-provenance.concern: What produced a server run: the build, its git commit, and the settings that shape the run, as lines of a name and a value that the program words.
kkt-provenance.must_not: Store the run record: kkt-rules' `start` does.

kkt-scratch.concern: Tests' scratch folders under `target/tmp`, named for the test and removed when dropped.

kkt-api-sim.concern: A simulated application, for tests and the web preview: `Preview`, which implements the kkt-api crates' contracts the web page uses over a world made up from a seed, answering `limits` with its own values, and `PreviewGate`, a stand-in for kkt-web's `Gate`, with an access key (checked by kkt-admission's check) or open. All of it is behind `testing`.
kkt-api-sim.must_not: Be in a release, or anything but a stand-in.

kkt-lane-files-os.concern: The machine's files and git for lane folders: plain OsDisk methods, adapted by the program.
kkt-lane-files-os.must_not: Decide which lanes to import or export.

kkt-clock-system.concern: The real wall clock and its sleep: SystemClock implements the shared Clock contract.

kkt-shutdown-os.concern: The operating system's stop signals, stopping the shared Shutdown value.
kkt-shutdown-os.must_not: Let a tokio signal type out of the crate.

kkt-service-os.concern: The machine's service files and commands: plain OsSystem methods, adapted by the program.
kkt-service-os.must_not: Decide what a service command does.

kinds.title: contract
kinds.about: Traits and plain values, with pure behaviour on its own value types (such as Time arithmetic, query checks and search matching), and no effect or wiring.

kinds.title: logic
kinds.about: Behaviour, with every effect injected. Protocol translation counts as logic.

kinds.title: effect
kinds.about: Touches the operating system, disk, network, real time or real randomness directly.

kinds.title: mixed
kinds.about: A contract or logic together with a real effect. The current map only: in the proposed map, a mixed crate is a violation.
